name: HRV sleep staging benchmark dataset
description: Automated sleep stage classification using heart-rate variability is an active field of research. In this work limitations of the current state-of-the-art are addressed through the use of deep learning techniques and their efficacy is demonstrated. First, a temporal model is proposed for the inference of sleep stages from electrocardiography using a deep long- and short-term (LSTM) classifier and it is shown that this model outperforms previous approaches which were often limited to non-temporal or Markovian classifiers on a comprehensive benchmark data set (292 participants, 541214 samples) comprising a wide range of ages and pathological profiles, achieving a Cohen's $κ$ of $0.61\pm0.16$ and accuracy of $76.30\pm10.17$ annotated according to the Rechtschaffen & Kales annotation standard. reputation: A research benchmark used in sleep-stage classification studies, especially for ECG/HRV-based modeling and transfer learning, but not a mainstream public leaderboard benchmark.
notes: Clinical time-series benchmark with subject-level variability and class imbalance; reported performance is often sensitive to annotation standard, split protocol, and patient heterogeneity.
